title: DEFAG and the possible 14-letter answer
hypothesis: The earlier offering names might preserve a musical sequence or a paired name-length pattern.
investigated: I compared the five offering names in riddle order, the Journal layout and the earlier DEFAG playback report.
why: R1 already uses word initials. The five offering initials give DEFAG, and their letter-only lengths are 18, 18, 15, 15 and 14.

evidence.label: Observed
evidence.text: The initials and lengths are reproducible observations about the named offerings. They are separate patterns, not independent proof of one decoder.

evidence.label: Reported
evidence.text: exomechs already reported playing D E F A G with Melody’s Hair. The report does not supply a complete per-action outcome, register or stage record.

against: Neither pattern identifies what to assemble or why the body must be gone.
A 14-letter sixth answer is a prediction from two earlier pairs. It is not a discovered answer or a reason to shop for matching items.
assessment: I’m keeping the observations, but I’ve parked new playback and letter-count guesses until a source selects an operation.
next_evidence: An authentic Journal feature or game instruction selecting which information to combine would change this.

title: One chain, three pairs, or both?
hypothesis: Earlier steps might form pairs while still passing information or conditions into later riddles.
investigated: I compared the chain and pair readings against the documented R4/R5 relationship and the offering-name lengths.
why: R5 explicitly refers to past offerings, while the first four answer-name lengths form two equal adjacent pairs.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: The completed R5 entry requires three Callings already in the lake when the Griffin Feather arrives.

evidence.label: Interpretation
evidence.text: A pairing scheme and a chain can coexist. Neither model follows automatically from the other.

against: The use of Callings in both steps does not prove that untouched R4 item entities must carry over into R5.
Only the R4-to-R5 back-reference is directly established here. Extending it across every riddle is an extra assumption.
assessment: I’m keeping these models separate. I want a specific predicted relationship, not a structure that can fit any later answer.
next_evidence: A documented dependency between another pair of steps would help distinguish a general structure from one local back-reference.

title: Could earlier patches have prepared mechanics for the Dead Man’s Hunt?
hypothesis: Some mechanics may have been introduced or refined between the December 2025 election and the October 2026 launch, mixed into ordinary updates.
investigated: I checked original developer announcements for changes to Frozen Corpse loot, Wisp progression, Shaggy and the Arachne Crystal, salvage and Reforge Stones.
why: The working chronology places Dra2oon’s election in December 2025 and the Hunt launch on 6 October 2026: roughly ten months. That allows a preparation window, but does not establish when R6 was designed.

evidence.label: Reported
evidence.text: December 2025 is the working election month. This check did not locate an original developer record independently pinning down that date; the approximately ten-month interval remains qualified context.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: 18 February 2026 — the Alpha release candidate adds Caged Wisp to Frozen Corpse loot and documents the lantern-to-Will-o-wisp progression. This announcement date is not proof of the first live release date.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: 31 March 2026 — the live update adds Shaggy’s Abiphone contact, increases Crystal rarity and removes the rare-relic quest. The exact revised exchange quantities are documented separately on the Crystal reference page.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: 28 April 2026 — Caged Wisp becomes salvageable for 500 Fossil Essence. This is salvage output, not its shop price.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: 25 August 2026 — the original Alpha announcement already lists Hunt (Dra2oon), with its details redacted. It does not disclose when individual riddles were developed.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: 6 October 2026 — the Minister Update accompanies the Hunt and includes broad Reforge Stone changes: stats menus, textures, costs and rewritten bonus descriptions. Its full announcement was recovered for this review.

against: Progression, accessibility, salvage and clearer descriptions are independent reasons for these updates. Documented changes are not confirmed R6 clues.
The election-to-launch interval does not prove continuous R6 development, early implementation or a hidden purpose for any particular item.
No item-specific before-and-after exception has been established here that selects a completion action.
assessment: I’m keeping the preparation question open, with Needs verification status. The timeline is worth checking, but it does not justify reopening an old recipe or buying materials.
next_evidence: An original election-date record and a targeted, dated mechanic or text diff beyond the broad updates would help. More coinciding dates alone would not.

revisions.title: Were older mechanics refined for the Hunt?
revisions.hypothesis: A targeted pre-Hunt change could help identify the intended mechanic, if it differs from ordinary system-wide maintenance.
revisions.assessment: I’m keeping one narrow question open: is there a targeted exception to the broad updates? I haven’t found one that earns a gameplay test.
revisions.note: Earlier wording retained when this timeline was expanded. Both reviews were documented on 15 November; no exact times are recorded.

title: What does “the body is not enough” actually require?
hypothesis: The clue may describe an incomplete object, an incomplete process or information the body cannot supply.
investigated: I separated three readings of insufficiency and checked whether the wording requires us to make a body disappear during the experiment.
why: A remains-based item can fit the last sentence while leaving the first sentence unexplained.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: R1 leaves a Journal after the Chestplate is consumed. The recovered Journal is already intact; this does not establish a Journal assembly recipe.

evidence.label: Interpretation
evidence.text: “Not enough” denies sufficiency. It does not prove the body is a required ingredient. “When it is gone” can also describe an already absent body.

against: The grammatical possibilities do not select one object or native operation.
R4 specifies an insufficient first and second call. R6 supplies no equivalent explicit count, so adding one needs separate evidence.
assessment: I’m prioritizing source text that explains the missing relationship. I haven’t selected another item offering from this wording alone.
next_evidence: A native instruction explaining why an original object is insufficient and what surviving material or information completes it would be the useful connection.

title: Checking Arachne’s native assembly chain
hypothesis: Arachne’s drops can fund a manufactured Crystal, giving a concrete process beyond simply offering a body-related item.
investigated: I selected a bounded source check of the boss-drop-to-Crystal interpretation and its existing exchange reports.
why: R4 and R5 already use Arachne’s Callings, and Shaggy’s exchange is an actual assembly-like interaction.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: The documented exchange uses two Arachne Fragments, sixteen Enchanted Spider Eyes and sixteen Enchanted String.

evidence.label: Reported
evidence.text: Collin already reported a remote Shaggy exchange in the lake followed by offering the Crystal. This is more than a finished-item throw.

against: The exchange report lacks an independent before-and-after Journal capture.
The clue never names Arachne, and having a recipe does not establish that the Hunt detects that exchange.
assessment: I thought this deserved a focused source check before any further gameplay. I did not treat it as a new discovery or an untested procedure.
next_evidence: Check whether the actual lore selects a materially different operation from the reported exchange and offering.

title: Arachne: no new operation selected
hypothesis: The Crystal interpretation needs evidence distinguishing it from ordinary boss progression and the exchange procedure already reported.
investigated: I checked the Fragment and Crystal descriptions, Shaggy’s transcribed dialogue and the existing exchange-then-offer report.
why: The earlier review left open whether native text supplied a missing relationship between the body, surviving power and assembly.

evidence.label: Confirmed
evidence.text: Callings summon Arachne; boss-dropped Fragments are different items used in the Crystal exchange. Two surviving Callings are not the recipe’s two Fragments.

evidence.label: Observed
evidence.text: Fragment lore describes Arachne’s power, while the Crystal summons her true strength. The inspected text does not describe rebuilding her corpse.

evidence.label: Reported
evidence.text: Collin’s report covers a lake exchange while wearing 8/8 Arachne gear, then offering the Crystal. It still lacks independent stage and Journal proof.

against: One ordinary drop being too few for a recipe does not independently select two fresh kills as an R6 condition.
Shaggy’s dialogue transcription retains old costs, while the item pages document revised costs. That inconsistency does not establish another usable recipe.
assessment: I’ve parked this route. Its connection to earlier steps is real, but I found no source-based reason to add fresh-kill history, timing or another offering.
next_evidence: Reopen only for authentic text or an unexplained observation selecting a different action, or a correction that materially changes the existing report’s coverage.
